request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Each claim row lists one line per status it has had, oldest first, as `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`. Adding a claim writes its DRAFT line, and every status change (open, settle, approve, reject, void) writes another. The due is taken at the moment of the change, the same figure the screen shows: any statement binding and late charge are included, and it reads `n/a` when no rate applies. A refused change writes no line.

What changed:
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V29__claim_log.sql` adds a `claim_log` table, read and written through `ClaimLog` and `ClaimLogRepository`.
- **Server:** a new step, `LogClaimStatus`, runs right after the audit step in three endpoints: adding a claim, quick-add, and changing a claim's status. Every claim the server returns now carries its `log`, and the full claims list loads all of the sheet's log lines in one query.
- **Front end:** the `log` field is added to the `Claim` type in `claims.ts`. In `list.slot.tsx` each claim row renders the lines as `claim-log` / `claim-log-line`.

Editing a draft or moving a claim to another person writes no line, since neither changes the status. Claims created before this migration will show an empty log.
